levels.title: Planet Earth in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can name Earth's continents and oceans and say how much of the surface is water.

levels.title: Why Every Map Is Wrong
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why every flat map distorts the round Earth and compare two common projections.

levels.title: Latitude and Longitude
levels.objective: After this level you can find any place on Earth using latitude and longitude.

levels.title: The Equator and the Tropics
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the Equator, the tropics and the polar circles mark and why they sit where they do.

levels.title: Time Zones
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why the world has time zones and where the calendar date changes.

levels.title: Compass and Directions
levels.objective: After this level you can use the cardinal directions and explain how a compass finds north.

levels.title: Reading the Land
levels.objective: After this level you can read elevation on a map and name landforms like plateaus, valleys and deltas.

levels.title: Continents and Oceans by Size
levels.objective: After this level you can rank the seven continents and five oceans by size.

levels.title: How Your Phone Knows Where You Are
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how satellites let a phone pinpoint its location.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Reading the Planet
levels.objective: After this level you can use maps, coordinates, directions and time zones together to describe where any place is.

levels.title: Inside the Earth
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Earth's crust, mantle and core.

levels.title: Plate Tectonics
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how moving plates reshape continents over millions of years.

levels.title: Pangaea
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the evidence that today's continents were once joined.

levels.title: Earthquakes
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what causes earthquakes and how their size is measured.

levels.title: Volcanoes and the Ring of Fire
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why volcanoes form where they do and locate the Ring of Fire.

levels.title: Tsunamis
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how undersea earthquakes cause tsunamis and why they are so destructive.

levels.title: How Mountains Rise
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how colliding plates build mountain ranges like the Himalayas.

levels.title: The Rock Cycle
levels.objective: After this level you can name the three kinds of rock and explain how one turns into another.

levels.title: Wind, Water and Ice
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how erosion carves canyons, valleys and coastlines.

levels.title: Checkpoint: The Restless Earth
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how moving plates build mountains and cause earthquakes, volcanoes and tsunamis.

levels.title: The Water Cycle
levels.objective: After this level you can describe how water moves between the ocean, the sky and the land.

levels.title: One World Ocean
levels.objective: After this level you can name the five oceans and explain why they are really one connected ocean.

levels.title: Ocean Currents
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how currents like the Gulf Stream carry heat around the planet.

levels.title: Coasts and Beaches
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how waves build and wear away coastlines.

levels.title: Great Rivers
levels.objective: After this level you can compare the Nile, the Amazon and other great rivers by length and flow.

levels.title: Lakes and Inland Seas
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how lakes form and why some, like the Dead Sea, are salty.

levels.title: Glaciers and Ice Sheets
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how glaciers form and how much fresh water they hold.

levels.title: Fresh Water Is Rare
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how little of Earth's water is fresh and easy to reach.

levels.title: River Valleys and the First Farms
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why river valleys and deltas drew the first farms and cities.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Water World
levels.objective: After this level you can trace water through the oceans, rivers, ice and the water cycle.

levels.title: Weather or Climate?
levels.objective: After this level you can tell weather from climate and explain why the difference matters.

levels.title: Why the Equator Is Hot
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the angle of sunlight makes the tropics warm and the poles cold.

levels.title: Wind and Pressure
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how differences in air pressure make wind, including the trade winds.

levels.title: Rain Shadows
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why one side of a mountain range can be wet and the other dry.

levels.title: Monsoons
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how seasonal winds bring monsoon rains to South Asia.

levels.title: Hurricanes and Typhoons
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how tropical storms form and why they have different names in different oceans.

levels.title: Thunderstorms and Tornadoes
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how thunderstorms, lightning and tornadoes form.

levels.title: Climate Zones
levels.objective: After this level you can name the main climate zones and say where on Earth each one occurs.

levels.title: A Changing Climate
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the greenhouse effect and how Earth's climate is changing today.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Climate and Weather
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how sunlight, wind, water and mountains combine to make weather and climate.

levels.title: What Is a Biome?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a biome is and how climate shapes it.

levels.title: Rainforests
levels.objective: After this level you can describe tropical rainforests and explain why they hold so many species.

levels.title: Deserts
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why deserts form and why not all of them are hot.

levels.title: Grasslands and Savannas
levels.objective: After this level you can describe grasslands and savannas and the animals they support.

levels.title: Forests of the North
levels.objective: After this level you can describe temperate and northern forests and how they survive winter.

levels.title: Tundra
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the tundra and the frozen ground beneath it.

levels.title: Climbing Through Climates
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how climate and life change as you climb a mountain.

levels.title: Coral Reefs
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what coral reefs are and why they are so fragile.

levels.title: Wetlands
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what wetlands do for water and wildlife.

levels.title: Milestone: The Physical World
levels.objective: After this level you can connect landforms, water, climate and biomes into one picture of how Earth works.

levels.title: Africa in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Africa's size and how its landscapes change from north to south.

levels.title: The Sahara
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Sahara and how it has changed over thousands of years.

levels.title: The Nile
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Nile made farming and cities possible in Egypt.

levels.title: The Great Rift Valley
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Great Rift Valley formed and why it matters to the story of human origins.

levels.title: Kilimanjaro and Africa's Peaks
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Africa's highest mountains and their shrinking ice.

levels.title: The Congo Basin
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Congo rainforest and the river that drains it.

levels.title: Africa's Countries and Cities
levels.objective: After this level you can name Africa's most populous countries and largest cities.

levels.title: The Middle East
levels.objective: After this level you can locate the Middle East and describe its deserts, rivers and seas.

levels.title: Oil and Water
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why oil and fresh water shape life in the Middle East.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Africa and the Middle East
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the main landscapes, rivers and resources of Africa and the Middle East.

levels.title: Europe in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Europe's shape, seas and main regions.

levels.title: The Alps and Europe's Rivers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Alps and rivers like the Rhine and Danube shaped Europe.

levels.title: The Mediterranean
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the Mediterranean's climate and why the sea connected ancient peoples.

levels.title: Russia, the Biggest Country
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Russia's size, Siberia and its eleven time zones.

levels.title: Asia in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Asia's regions and why most people on Earth live there.

levels.title: The Himalayas
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Himalayas, Mount Everest and the great rivers they feed.

levels.title: China's Great Rivers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Yangtze and the Yellow River shaped China.

levels.title: India and South Asia
levels.objective: After this level you can describe South Asia's landscapes, its monsoon and its huge population.

levels.title: Islands of Fire
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Japan, Indonesia and the Philippines have so many volcanoes and earthquakes.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Europe and Asia
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the main mountains, rivers and regions of Europe and Asia.

levels.title: North America in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can describe North America's regions from the Arctic to Central America.

levels.title: The Rockies and the Great Plains
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Rockies and the Great Plains divide the continent.

levels.title: The Mississippi
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Mississippi river system drains the middle of North America.

levels.title: The Great Lakes
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Great Lakes and how glaciers carved them.

levels.title: The Grand Canyon
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon.

levels.title: Mexico and Central America
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the volcanoes, highlands and coasts of Mexico and Central America.

levels.title: The Caribbean
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Caribbean islands and explain their hurricane season.

levels.title: South America in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can describe South America's regions and largest countries.

levels.title: The Amazon and the Andes
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Andes and the Amazon shape South America.

levels.title: Checkpoint: The Americas
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the main mountains, rivers and regions of North and South America.

levels.title: Australia in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Australia's dry interior and explain where most Australians live.

levels.title: Uluru and the Outback
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Outback and what Uluru means to Aboriginal Australians.

levels.title: The Great Barrier Reef
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Great Barrier Reef and the threats it faces.

levels.title: New Zealand
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how moving plates shaped New Zealand's mountains and hot springs.

levels.title: The Pacific Islands
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how volcanoes and coral built the islands of the Pacific.

levels.title: Wayfinders of the Pacific
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Polynesian navigators crossed the Pacific by reading stars, waves and birds.

levels.title: The Arctic
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Arctic Ocean and its shrinking sea ice.

levels.title: Antarctica
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Antarctica is the coldest, driest and windiest continent.

levels.title: Who Owns Antarctica?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the Antarctic Treaty and what it protects.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Oceania and the Poles
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Australia, the Pacific islands, the Arctic and Antarctica.

levels.title: Eight Billion People
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the world population grew and where people live today.

levels.title: Cities
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why cities grow and name the largest urban areas.

levels.title: Countries and Borders
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how borders are drawn and why the count of countries varies.

levels.title: Languages of the World
levels.objective: After this level you can name the world's most spoken languages and explain language families.

levels.title: Religions Around the World
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the world's major religions and where they are practiced.

levels.title: Feeding the World
levels.objective: After this level you can explain where the world's food is grown and which crops feed the most people.

levels.title: Resources and Wealth
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how resources like oil, metals and water shape where wealth is found.

levels.title: People on the Move
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why people migrate and where the biggest movements happen.

levels.title: Humans Change the Planet
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how farming, cities and pollution reshape the land and the sea.

levels.title: Mastery Challenge: World Geography
levels.objective: After this level you can demonstrate command of World Geography Levels 1–99 across the whole tree.
